properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.77.0): the missing-argument refusal looks up a field's description only among the schema's TOP-LEVEL properties. So a required field missing inside an array item is reported as if it were top-level and "its own schema publishes no description of it" — false for 22 of the 35 nested required fields on the surface. The guard every_required_parameter_is_described.rs walks the same top level, so it misses the 13 that really have no description
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, triage agent B. Items F-add_decision and F-set_artifact_checksums of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02.

① OBSERVED, reproduced verbatim on 0.77.0 through `--call`, on a scratch store:
- add_decision with related_to [{other_id, relation}] exits 2 with: "`add_decision` was called without the required argument `evidence`. Its own schema publishes no description of it, so what it wants cannot be quoted here."
- set_artifact_checksums with accepts [{artifact_id, checksum}] gives the same sentence for `disposition`.
EXPECTED: the refusal quotes the field's description, says the field belongs to an item of `related_to` / `accepts`, and for disposition names its three values on the FIRST refusal.

② PRECEDENT: cap:a-missing-field-refusal-names-the-fields-this-call-lacked (realized 2026-09-19) and epoch:a-missing-argument-names-the-tool-and-what-it-wants built the hint. Nothing records the nested case.

⑤ MEASURED:
- In code: missing_fields_hint's brief() reads `schema["properties"][field]["description"]` only (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs ~238, origin/main 66620f7). It never follows `items.$ref` into `$defs`.
- In the published schemas: add_decision's $defs.RelationLinkReq.evidence HAS a description ("WHY this relation is true, in a sentence…"). $defs.ChecksumAcceptReq.disposition HAS one that names design_holds / design_updated / baseline_established. So the refusal's claim is false in both cases.
- Swept over all 195 tools' tools/list schemas: 16 tools carry $defs, with 35 required nested fields. 22 have descriptions, for which the refusal is FALSE. 13 have none, for which it is true but undetected.
- The guard crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/every_required_parameter_is_described.rs builds its membership from `schema["properties"]` too, so the 13 have never been seen by it.
- No nested field name collides with a top-level one, so all 35 fall to the false/undetected branch.

⑥ CLASS: the instrument (the refusal) and the check (the guard) share one blind spot, a top-level-only schema walk. A fix to the refusal alone leaves 13 undescribed fields unpinned. A fix that resolves $ref in both closes the class.

THE REPORT'S CONCLUSION CORRECTED: "set_artifact_checksums disposition values appear only after passing a wrong one" is true in effect, but the cause is this hint. The values ARE published, as prose in the item's description rather than as an enum. The first refusal would have quoted them if it read $defs.

Not established: whether a `type: string` field documented only in prose should carry an enum. chg:enum-fields-publish-their-legal-values-from-the-schema covers values sourced from the design schema, and disposition is not one of those.
